violations.why: ISR can write v_vessel between the write in fn_summit and the read in fn_juniper, creating a write‑write‑read race.
The task writes v_vessel at line 22, ISR may write it before fn_juniper reads it at line 33, yielding a write‑write‑read violation.
fn_juniper reads v_vessel then ISR can write it before fn_juniper writes v_vessel, forming a read‑write‑write race.
ISR can write v_vessel between the read in fn_juniper and the later read in fn_nectar, giving a read‑write‑read violation.
After fn_juniper writes v_vessel, ISR may write it again before fn_nectar reads it, causing a write‑write‑read race.
ISR can write v_vessel between the read in fn_nectar and the later read at line 29, producing a read‑write‑read violation.
The write in fn_summit can be interrupted by ISR before fn_nectar reads v_vessel, yielding a write‑write‑read race.
ISR may write v_vessel between the fn_summit write and the final read at line 29, creating a write‑write‑read violation.
The task's write at line 22 can be pre‑empted by ISR before fn_nectar reads v_vessel, resulting in a write‑write‑read race.
ISR can intervene between the write at line 22 and the later read at line 29, causing a write‑write‑read atomicity violation.
After fn_juniper writes v_vessel, ISR may overwrite it before the final read at line 29, forming a write‑write‑read violation.
ISR can write v_vessel between the early read in fn_juniper and the later read at line 29, leading to a read‑write‑read race.
